label: Motion Offence - a rule-based, read-and-react system
definition: Motion is not a play but a set of rules executed at pace: pass and cut, screen away, fill the vacant spot, backdoor the overplay, and make half-second decisions. The graph below models the canonical sequence (pass -> cut -> fill -> screen away -> read -> attack), with the branch point on how the defender plays the cut.

key: Pass and cut: every pass is followed by movement by the passer
Fill from the bottom: never leave two players in one spot
Backdoor a defender who overplays; basket-cut a defender who relaxes
Half-second decisions: catch, read, shoot-pass-drive
One player per spot: the corners must be occupied at all times
Motion is a spacing offence: it fails the moment two players share an area

nodes.label: Motion Offence
nodes.definition: A continuous, rule-based offensive sequence rather than a scripted play.

nodes.label: Set the five spots
nodes.definition: One player at the top, two on the wings and two in the corners (5-out); or four on the arc with a dive man on the weak-side block (4-out-1-in).

key: Spacing is the system: five spots, five players, no exceptions
The corners are the most valuable real estate on the floor

nodes.label: Pass the ball
nodes.definition: Move the ball with a purpose: pass to a teammate who is in a position to shoot, drive or pass again. The pass initiates the read for everyone else.

key: Pass to score, not to relocate the problem
Ball reversal is the cheapest way to break a set defence

nodes.label: Cut after the pass
nodes.definition: The passer does not admire his pass: he cuts hard to the rim, or screens away for a teammate who will cut into his spot.

key: Cut to score: run to the rim with the intention of catching the ball
Sell the cut: change of pace and a hand target

nodes.label: Fill the vacant spot
nodes.definition: The passer has cut, so the next player up fills the spot he vacated, keeping the five spots occupied and the spacing honest.

key: Fill from the bottom: the nearest player to the ball fills first
Motion dies the moment two players occupy one spot

nodes.label: Read how the defender plays the cut
nodes.definition: The branch point: a defender who trails the cut is beaten by continuing it; a defender who overplays the passing lane is beaten behind him.

props.condition: position and attention of the cutter's defender
key: Read the defender's chest, not the ball
The decision is made in half a second: catch, read, go

nodes.label: Finish the basket cut
nodes.definition: The defender has relaxed or turned his head: continue the cut to the rim for a lay-up or a duck-in feed.

key: Cut rim-to-rim, not to the ball
Present a target hand and get your feet set if the ball is late

nodes.label: Backdoor the overplay
nodes.definition: The defender is denying the passing lane: cut behind him to the rim, and the passer hits him on the backdoor.

key: One hard fake to the ball, then go behind
The passer must wait for the cut to clear the defender's hip

nodes.label: Relocate to an open spot
nodes.definition: The cut is not on, so move to a new spot on the arc (usually lifting to the wing or drifting to the corner) and stay shot-ready.

key: Move on the flight of the pass, not after the catch
Relocate to a spot where you can shoot, not to a spot where you are merely open

nodes.label: Screen away from the ball
nodes.definition: While the ball is on one side, the weak-side players screen for each other: a down screen to free a shooter to the corner, or a flare screen to free him to the wing.

key: Screen the man who is being watched, not the man who is watching the ball
Screener then re-screens or pops: never screen and stand

nodes.label: Screener re-screens or pops
nodes.definition: After setting the screen, the screener either re-screens for the same teammate or pops to the arc, keeping the action alive instead of standing.

key: The second screen is often the one that works
Pop with your hands ready: the pass may come immediately

nodes.label: Dribble hand-off or dribble-at
nodes.definition: The receiver of the screen either hands the ball off to the cutter or attacks the closeout with a dribble hand-off, forcing the defence to defend a moving screen and a new ball handler at once.

key: A hand-off to a shooter is a screen and a pass in one motion
The hand-off receiver must be a shooting or driving threat, or the defence just switches it

nodes.label: Drive the closeout and kick it out
nodes.definition: Attack a recovering closeout, draw the collapse, and kick the ball to the relocated shooter on the arc.

key: Attack the shoulder of the closeout, not the chest
The kick-out is the shot, not the drive: the drive is the setup

nodes.label: Crash the glass or retreat to safety
nodes.definition: On the shot, two players crash the offensive boards while two retreat to protect against transition, and the shooter sprints back.

key: Crash from the perimeter, where no one is blocking you out
Never send all five to the glass: transition defence is the price
